deviations.what: The controller's Formatting.setCustomCurrencies({BGN4:{digits:4}, WWWW:{digits:5}}) is carried as a follow_up_action( cs_event-control_global, FORMATTING/setCustomCurrencies ) with the same JSON payload. **Corrected 2026-08-23 - the digit counts are NOT reproduced, and were never going to be.** Two separate reasons, both measured. (1) The framework asked for the module as sap/ui/core/Formatting, which no UI5 release ships (the module is sap/base/i18n/Formatting), so sap.ui.require returned undefined and the action logged 'FORMATTING.setCustomCurrencies not available' and did nothing. Fixed upstream on that date - this port is where it was found. (2) Even with the right module the call cannot reach THIS control: the original registers the currencies in onInit, before the view exists, while a client action necessarily runs after the response is rendered, and sap.ui.unified.Currency caches its NumberFormat in init( ) (Currency.js: this._oFormat = NumberFormat.getCurrencyInstance) and implements no _handleLocalizationChange - so the cached formatter keeps the CLDR digits. A BOUND sap.ui.model.type.Currency does implement that hook and does re-format, which is what the capability is good for. So list five renders BGN4 and WWWW with the default 2 decimals where the original shows 4 and 5. The residual in the deviation beside this one was right all along; this text was not.

The various/nonDecimal arrays back the u:Currency value property (float) as ABAP packed fields, matching the sample's JSON numbers; the bigNumber array (JSON strings) and the customCurrency array (JSON numbers bound to the string property stringValue, so UI5 coerces them) are ABAP string fields keeping the exact literals (123.45676 has 5 decimals). listSix binds the numeric variousNumberDataModel/price to stringValue (number coerced to string, as in the original). **e2e-verified 2026-08-01** (scripts/e2e-smoke.mjs interaction, transpiled backend + real browser): the serialized model reaches the controls: the lists render, the u:Currency controls come up and their currencies (EUR, JPY) are on screen. Residual: the exact digit formatting per list (maxPrecision, the custom BGN4/WWWW digits), which is the browser's locale formatting rather than the port's data.
